html:
October 23, 2026

Israel orders West Bank closure after deadly attack near Hebron

tags: politics, conflict
sources: @groundnews, @oafnation_actual, @total.hypocrisy

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the military to impose a closure on Hebron and prepare a full lockdown of the occupied West Bank after an attack near the city, with all gates and checkpoints reported closed as of early afternoon local time. Israeli accounts say Palestinian gunmen killed two soldiers and wounded three others before both attackers were killed, while Netanyahu announced evacuations from the attackers' neighbourhood, house-to-house weapons searches and extensive arrests; Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich ordered demolitions near the attack site and called for a Gaza-style campaign including dismantling the Palestinian Authority. The closure leaves roughly 3.5 million people confined where they are, which critics describe as collective punishment, and it comes four days before Israel's October 27 parliamentary election. One account on the ground disputes the official version, saying no Israeli soldiers were killed and that settlers and the IDF confronted Palestinians during an olive harvest.

US troops describe destroyed bases and abandoned families in Iran war

tags: war, defence
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell

Service members at US bases across the Middle East provided previously unpublished photographs and video showing destroyed aircraft and bombed barracks, obtained by the Valor Media Network and published with MeidasTouch. Sources said Iranian missiles and drones struck US barracks in Jordan in July, with troops trapped inside fires, while personnel in the United Arab Emirates said they learned of the war from television, had no shelters and dug their own foxholes. In Bahrain, families said evacuation aircraft were available but the Pentagon declined to send them because it would make the situation look bad domestically. Service members said they had been used as pawns and that the war shows no sign of concluding.

Trump suggests renewed strikes on Iran after the midterms

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Speaking at a rally in Sioux City, President Donald Trump indicated the war with Iran could resume after the midterm elections, saying "we may do it a little bit further," according to CNN. Officials told the network that advisers have drawn up plans for renewed strikes alongside Israel, with the so-called "mother of all bombs" under consideration. Iowa Republican voters were described as wary of escalation, and Senate nominee Hinson called for a "successful and immediate end" to the conflict. Two Iowa soldiers have died in the war.

Iran reports seven vessels struck or damaged near Strait of Hormuz

tags: war, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Iran's Revolutionary Guard said four vessels caught fire and three others struck naval mines near the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran also threatened a wider response against American military bases if US forces continue facilitating shipping through the waterway. The seven reported incidents have not been independently confirmed.

Justice Department declines to rule out intervening in state certification

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas, @total.hypocrisy

Attorney General Todd Blanche was asked whether there is any scenario in which the Justice Department would weigh in on or try to block states from certifying election results. He said it is not and never has been the department's intention to improperly interfere with elections or state certification processes, but declined to say there are no circumstances under which it would do so, citing hypothetical doomsday scenarios. States, not the federal government, certify elections, and advocates said leaving the door open raises the prospect of federal interference and major legal challenges.

Administration sues to block Alaska Senate certification if Republican loses

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

The Trump administration has filed suit seeking to prevent certification of Alaska's Senate race in the event the Republican incumbent loses. The case turns on multiple candidates appearing on the ballot under the name Dan Sullivan, which is also the name of the sitting Republican senator. The suit asks a court to bar the state from certifying if Democrat Mary Peltola wins and the number of ballots cast for the other Dan Sullivan would have been enough to give the incumbent a win. The filing is preemptive, coming before results are public.

Warning of a post-midterm constitutional crisis over delayed certifications

tags: politics, legal
sources: @total.hypocrisy

A detailed timeline traces Justice Department efforts since January 2025 to obtain voter rolls from all 50 states and Washington DC, lawsuits against non-complying states including Oregon, Maine and later Connecticut and 22 others, a March 31, 2026 executive order tightening mail-in voting rules, and dismissals of DOJ cases by judges in Maine, Wisconsin, Michigan and Pennsylvania. Letters sent to election officials warned of possible criminal charges over non-citizens on voter rolls, and the department directed states to retain 2024 election records past the 22-month retention mark; in mid-September the Supreme Court declined to let the USPS enforce a mail ballot rule. The scenario outlined is that after the November 3 midterms, DOJ investigations and FBI seizures of ballots and records could delay certification in selected counties, leaving House races uncertified when the new Congress is seated in January. In that scenario the House clerk could be replaced with a loyalist who omits uncertified Democratic winners from the roll, producing competing claims to the majority and a standoff if courts order the certified winners seated.

State Department accused of screening diplomats by how they voted

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Eric Katz of the Washington Sun reported that the State Department has begun asking career diplomats up for promotion whether they voted for Donald Trump in 2016, 2020 and 2024. The department said it is screening for "fidelity and execution of the President's vision," and top officials reportedly told candidates that only those who voted for Trump would be eligible for mid- to upper-level foreign service roles and that campaign donation histories would be examined, with donations to Democrats disqualifying. Federal law prohibits hiring and promotion decisions in the civil service based on political belief.

Election interference efforts failing in court, officials say

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas

The administration has lost more than 20 lawsuits concerning voter rolls, and claims that hundreds of thousands of non-citizens were voting have not been substantiated. Utah reviewed more than 2 million records and found 52 questionable ones, while Nevada checked a list of 185 alleged non-citizens and found all 185 were citizens. Elections are run by states, voting machines are tested by federally accredited labs before purchase and around each election, identities and mail ballot signatures are verified, nearly all ballots leave a paper record, precincts are reconciled and nearly every state audits results before certification. Voters in most states can track their ballots online.

Pentagon whistleblowers prepare to testify against Hegseth

tags: politics, defence
sources: @aaronparnas

Reporting from the Independent and the Telegraph says House Democrats have begun contacting potential Pentagon whistleblowers who are prepared to "spill their guts" if a congressional investigation into Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is launched. Hegseth is described as the top target for congressional Democrats, who may pursue impeachment or wide-ranging investigations. A number of people inside the Pentagon are reportedly willing to speak.

Supreme Court leaves block on transgender inmate care restrictions in place

tags: legal, health
sources: @groundnews

The Supreme Court rejected an emergency request from the Trump administration to enforce restrictions on gender-affirming care for transgender federal prisoners, leaving a lower court's block in place while litigation continues. The policy, introduced in February, would prohibit hormone treatments, surgeries and accommodations such as clothing and hair-removal devices; 2025 government figures count more than 2,000 transgender inmates in federal facilities and halfway houses. A federal judge blocked the policy in June, finding it likely violated federal administrative law and disregarded the prison system's medical experience. The court gave no explanation, and Justices Clarence Thomas and Samuel Alito dissented.

Ilhan Omar to leave her home after threats following federal raid

tags: politics, immigration
sources: @groundnews

Representative Ilhan Omar said she plans to leave her Washington, DC apartment after receiving death threats in the wake of a federal immigration fraud investigation. Agents searched her residence on October 12 and confiscated 17 items including her phone and other electronic devices. President Trump has accused Omar's father of falsifying her age during her 2000 citizenship process, which she denies; the Washington Post reported that a 2019 federal review found no evidence of immigration fraud. Omar described the investigation as a campaign of political intimidation and said publication of her address has endangered her family.

Trump defends Ramaswamy ad using estranged mother of Amy Acton

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

President Trump publicly backed an advertisement from Vivek Ramaswamy, the Republican nominee for governor of Ohio, that features Dr. Amy Acton's mother, from whom Acton has been estranged since age 12 after suffering abuse in the household. In a post on Truth Social, Trump called it a powerful ad, said Ramaswamy should keep it running, accused Acton of lying about the abuse and criticised Republicans including Ohio Governor Mike DeWine who had called for its removal. In separately surfaced audio, Ramaswamy was confronted at an Ohio child care centre and described Acton as "flawed" for having survived child sexual abuse. At the White House, Trump defended the ad again and attacked an NBC reporter who asked whether the abuse allegations mattered to him, calling her a "horrible little reporter."

Missouri ballot measure would reinstate abortion ban

tags: politics, health
sources: @aaronparnas

Missouri lawmakers are advancing Amendment 3, a ballot measure that would repeal the reproductive rights protections voters approved two years ago and effectively reinstate the state's abortion ban. The earlier vote ended a ban that had been described as among the most restrictive in the country. The measure is moving now with little national attention.

Global markets lose trillions in sell-off dubbed Black Thursday

tags: markets, tech
sources: @ericmoutsos

About $1 trillion was wiped from Asian stock markets and nearly $800 billion from US markets in a sell-off that spread globally, with losses put at over $10 trillion, on the anniversary of the 1987 Black Monday crash. The sell-off coincided with what is described as one of the largest cyber incidents in recent memory, with WordPress, Palo Alto and more than 400 banks primarily in Latin America reporting attacks over 24 hours, and US banks detecting unauthorised third-party AI agents conducting man-in-the-middle interception of credentials and two-factor authentication at institutions including JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Bank of America and Citibank. Two critical bugs were reported in PHP, a language running roughly 70% of websites, with disclosure credited to OpenAI and Google's Gemini and exploitation attributed to automated agents built after the news broke early. Prediction markets put the odds of US government confirmation of the vulnerability by Halloween at 93%, and the episode is being linked to Trump's statement that the government will take ownership stakes in OpenAI, Anthropic and other AI companies.

Quest Diagnostics breached, patient data accessed

tags: privacy, health
sources: @aaronparnas

Quest Diagnostics disclosed an incident involving unauthorized access to its Quanum Lab Services Manager system, which clients use to place test orders and retrieve results. The company paused access to the system and is investigating. It believes some patient data was accessed but says other systems were not affected, and is working to determine whose data was involved. The full scale of the breach is not yet known.

Kushner phone hack said to reveal Dubai account and transfers

tags: politics, legal
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

Reporting says Russian hackers accessed Jared Kushner's phone years ago, after which Dutch intelligence reverse-engineered the intrusion and flipped a Russian hacker to obtain the same access. The material reportedly showed Kushner had access to a Dubai-based bank account holding hundreds of millions of dollars, much of it originating from Azerbaijan, and that funds were transferred to a warlord, a hitman and a mercenary. Kushner has responded that the Vanity Fair account is a smear and entirely false.

Pentagon bans troops from betting on military operations

tags: defence, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Pentagon issued a directive prohibiting troops and civilian personnel from using nonpublic military information to place financial bets. It follows the prosecution of a Green Beret accused of turning roughly $33,000 in wagers on the Maduro operation into nearly $410,000 in profit. The directive warns that suspicious trading patterns could expose military operations to foreign adversaries.

Trump asks Musk to lift limits on Starshield service for Ukraine

tags: defence, tech
sources: @oafnation_actual

Trump called Elon Musk on Wednesday and asked him to fully reverse any limits on Starshield, the military version of Starlink that carries Ukraine's battlefield internet, according to the Wall Street Journal and the New York Post. Trump denied having ordered the slowdown. The system has improved since the call but is not yet back at full strength.

Appeals court finds switchblades protected by Second Amendment

tags: legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

A federal appeals court ruled that switchblade knives fall under Second Amendment protection. The Fifth Circuit found that longstanding federal restrictions on interstate manufacturing, transportation and distribution violate constitutional protections. The case returns to a lower court, and other federal restrictions and state knife laws are unaffected.

Army to spend $9 million restoring Arlington Confederate Memorial

tags: politics, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Army plans to spend approximately $9 million to restore the Confederate Memorial at Arlington National Cemetery. The sculpture was removed in 2023 and transferred to a private nonprofit in January 2026. The Army expects to reinstall it in 2027 using federal operations and maintenance funding.

Air Force veteran freed after four years in Russian custody

tags: politics, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old Air Force veteran, has returned to the United States after more than four years in Russian custody. His sister said he feared he would die there. He reportedly did not realise he had been freed until he boarded an aircraft and saw the American flag.

Prosecutors charge rehab operators in $1.6 billion fraud scheme

tags: legal, health
sources: @oafnation_actual

Federal prosecutors say operators of a large rehabilitation network drugged some patients to prevent them from leaving while submitting more than $1.6 billion in allegedly fraudulent insurance claims. Patients were reportedly offered flights, money and drugs, then cycled through facilities so billing could continue. Four people face federal charges.

Hegseth staff damaged Eisenhower's wartime globe during Pentagon move

tags: defence, politics
sources: @groundnews, @oafnation_actual

Staff working for Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth damaged a historic globe used by General Dwight D. Eisenhower during the Second World War while moving it to Hegseth's Pentagon office in February, three US officials told NBC News. The staffers attempted the move without help from Army historians and dropped the 1930s-era artifact onto its own mounting, leaving a several-inch hole near Antarctica. The globe, maintained by the US Army Center of Military History, carries Eisenhower's handwritten markings of locations across Europe. A Pentagon official acknowledged the accident but described the object as a replica undergoing repairs, while NBC News confirmed through three officials and photographic evidence that it was the original.

Navy offers EOD officers up to $100,000 to stay in uniform

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Navy is offering select explosive ordnance disposal officers up to $100,000 to remain in service for four more years. Eligible lieutenants generally need six years of commissioned service and lieutenant commanders ten. Two-year bonus options are also available under the program updated on October 20, and the incentives do not apply to every EOD technician.

Severe flooding hits Hurricane, Utah

tags: climate
sources: @ericmoutsos

Flooding in Hurricane, Utah on Thursday is described by residents as the worst since the 1980s, the second such flood in the town this year. The Hurricane Police Department ordered residents of the Willow Wind complex and homes along Gould's Wash to evacuate, with cars floating and homes inundated in the Gould's Wash area. The Navajo Police Department reminded residents not to drive through water-covered roads, warning the water can be deeper and faster-moving than it appears.

Trump says Google CEO talked him out of renaming the Atlantic Ocean

tags: politics, tech
sources: @groundnews

Speaking at a rally in South Carolina on Wednesday, President Trump said he had considered renaming the Atlantic Ocean after himself or America but dropped the idea after discussing it with Google CEO Sundar Pichai. Trump quoted Pichai as saying, "Oceans are different, sir. They cover really a lot of countries. Please don't ask us to do that." Google has not confirmed the conversation. Google Maps previously adopted federal name changes for the Gulf of Mexico and Lake Ontario for US users.

Concern raised over Trump's conduct at campaign events

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

Footage from a campaign appearance shows the president making an involuntary noise mid-sentence while speaking about control of the US Senate, then continuing his remarks. Commentators noted that similar incidents involving former President Joe Biden drew extensive coverage questioning his fitness and calls to invoke the 25th Amendment.
